findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name and verify the span-parenting mechanism (explicit parent-context capture vs ambient OTel context propagation) that guarantees candidate spans nest under the run-time Agent request span, given candidates are wrapped at construction time — spike it against the wired-but-unverified tracing seam before committing.
evidence: Approach: 'Instrument each already-built fallback or native-to-prompted candidate at the public Pydantic model boundary, preserving the Agent model-request span as the logical-turn parent.'
tracing.py:11 — 'This is wired but not live-verified (per the d6d1 decision)'
tracing.py:54 — 'Agent.instrument_all()  # emit agent/LLM/tool spans through the configured provider' (pydantic-ai owns the Agent/LLM span hierarchy)
Scope: 'wrap the concrete candidate models at construction' — construction-time context is not the run-time request context where the Agent span is active
ABSENCE: the plan names no explicit parent-context capture/propagation strategy to guarantee child nesting
findings.finding: The plan asserts candidate child spans will nest 'beneath one logical Agent request span' as parent, but does not state the mechanism by which rebar-emitted spans attach to the pydantic-ai-owned Agent request span. Candidate models are wrapped 'at construction' (runner setup), whereas the Agent request span only exists during the run; the OTel context active at wrap time differs from the context active during the candidate's actual request call, risking orphaned or mis-parented spans. This span-parenting capability is built on a seam tracing.py documents as 'wired but not live-verified' and should be spiked/verified before committing.
findings.location: Approach ('preserving the Agent model-request span as the logical-turn parent'); AC line 1 ('two ordered candidate spans beneath one logical Agent request span')
scenarios: Tracing enabled with a real OTLP or in-memory exporter: candidate spans emit as roots/orphans instead of children of the Agent request span, failing AC line 1's in-memory exporter test
Async run where the wrapped request executes under a different OTel context than the Agent-span-owning task

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the custom per-candidate span layer against pydantic-ai's existing InstrumentedModel/FallbackModel instrumentation (already active via Agent.instrument_all at tracing.py:54): state why framework-native fallback span handling is insufficient and how the new spans coexist without duplicating the standard gen_ai model-request spans.
evidence: Retrieved DeepWiki (deepwiki.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai) 'Observability and Instrumentation': 'The FallbackModel wrapper integrates with instrumentation to properly track which model succeeded and update span attributes accordingly.' and Instrumentation Architecture citing instrumented.py:510-520: 'FallbackModel handles instrumentation by ensuring the active span reflects the specific model that ultimately succeeded in a fallback sequence.'
Repo already relies on this framework-native path: src/rebar/llm/tracing.py:54 calls `Agent.instrument_all()` to 'emit agent/LLM/tool spans through the configured provider.'

ABSENCE: neither Context/Problem nor Approach names InstrumentedModel/instrument_all, explains why the framework-native fallback span handling is insufficient for the desired per-candidate visibility, nor states how the new custom spans coexist with instrument_all without duplicate or conflicting spans.
findings.finding: The plan proposes a novel custom per-candidate child-span layer at the Pydantic model boundary without considering pydantic-ai's existing InstrumentedModel/FallbackModel instrumentation, which already emits gen_ai spans per model request and already updates the active span to reflect the fallback model that succeeded.
findings.location: Approach — 'Instrument each already-built fallback or native-to-prompted candidate at the public Pydantic model boundary, preserving the Agent model-request span as the logical-turn parent.'
scenarios: Custom candidate spans and instrument_all both fire, producing duplicate/competing model-request spans under one Agent turn in Langfuse.
Framework already surfaces the succeeding fallback model on its own span, making part of the custom layer redundant.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prior-art note to Approach/Context comparing the framework-native InstrumentedModel/FallbackModel span behavior to the desired per-candidate child spans, and specify the coexistence contract (e.g. child spans nest under, and do not duplicate, the instrument_all model-request span).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the native-to-prompted framing: model_output_mode selection is a STATIC pre-run routing branch (structured.output_mode → one mode), not a runtime native-then-prompted candidate sequence; either drop the 'two candidate spans' claim for the downgrade or re-model it as an attribute/event on the single Agent request span recording the selected output mode and downgrade reason.
evidence: runner.py:102 — 'not a workaround for any forced-tool mechanism (none exists; output is selected by output_mode())'
structured.py:219-290 output_mode returns a single NativeOutput OR PromptedOutput mode object chosen from caps before the run
structured_run.py:116 — 'mode_obj = structured.output_mode(model_cls, caps, thinking=req.thinking)' called once, no native→prompted retry
The only reask loop (config.py:470, structured.py:367) is a parse-repair loop WITHIN the already-selected prompted path, not a native→prompted transition
findings.finding: The plan's native-to-prompted downgrade instrumentation describes a runtime two-attempt sequence ('native-raised then prompted-returned candidate outcomes') that does not exist in the code: structured.output_mode() statically selects EXACTLY ONE output mode (NativeOutput OR PromptedOutput) before the agent run, and runner.py:99-104 states plainly 'none exists; output is selected by output_mode()'. There is no runtime native attempt that raises and is then retried as prompted at the model boundary, so no 'native candidate span' can be emitted by observing that boundary.
findings.location: Approach paragraph; AC #3; Testing bullet 3 ('Native-schema rejection then prompted success yields two candidate spans')
scenarios: A native-capable model routed to PromptedOutput by schema-complexity or stack-support gates: this is a static routing decision, so no 'native-raised' outcome span occurs and AC #3's test would assert against a sequence that never happens.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe AC #3 to: 'When output_mode downgrades a native-capable model to PromptedOutput (schema complexity / stack support / thinking gate), the single Agent request span records a downgrade attribute (selected mode + reason) with no added Agent request and no second model attempt'; verify via output_mode/structured_run rather than a boundary-observed candidate sequence.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Separate the two mechanisms in the plan: keep FallbackModel candidate child-spans (real ordered runtime attempts) distinct from output-mode routing metadata (a static branch attribute on the request span), rather than treating both as 'candidates' at the model boundary.
evidence: model_classes.build_fallback_model builds N concrete Model objects wrapped by FallbackModel — a real runtime chain
output_mode selects one mode object, so there is no analogous set of ordered runtime attempts for the downgrade case
Conflating the two forces the downgrade AC into a 'two ordered candidate spans' shape that its control flow cannot produce
findings.finding: The plan applies one 'candidate span' abstraction to two structurally different phenomena — FallbackModel's genuine runtime multi-attempt chain vs the static output-mode routing branch — which weakens mechanism correctness and testability by asserting symmetric 'ordered candidate spans' for both. The FallbackModel half is sound (ordered real sub-models on one session, model_classes.py:428-434), but the downgrade half has no ordered runtime attempts to observe.
findings.location: Approach paragraph ('each already-built fallback or native-to-prompted candidate'); Scope bullet for model_classes.py
scenarios: A pure single-model op that merely gets routed to PromptedOutput: no FallbackModel exists, no candidate set exists, yet AC #3 expects 'two candidate spans'.
